description: A personal customer applies for a personal credit card through the bank's digital channel. The journey covers product selection, automated eligibility and credit check, instant decision, card issuance (virtual and physical), card activation, and entry into the ongoing credit card account management lifecycle. SVC-003 (Credit Card Service) owns the application and account lifecycle; SVC-012 (Risk Engine, CAP-004) provides hard credit scoring exclusively via async events; SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core, same capability) provides customer identity data via synchronous API.
happy_path_duration: Instant decision (< 5 minutes); virtual card issued same day; physical card 3–5 business days
regulatory_framework: Consumer Credit Act 1974 (CCA 1974) — Section 75 joint and several liability, right to withdraw (s66A), regulated credit agreement
FCA Consumer Credit sourcebook (CONC) — affordability, persistent debt (CONC 6.7.27–6.7.40), creditworthiness
FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9) — fair value, consumer understanding, consumer support, products and services outcomes
FCA CONC 5A — creditworthiness assessment and affordability
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0 (PCI DSS v4.0) — cardholder data environment, PAN tokenisation, PIN management
Payment Services Regulations 2017 (PSR 2017) — SCA for card activation and online card payments
FCA PS20/8 — persistent debt rules (CONC 6.7.27): bank must contact customers in persistent debt at 18, 27, and 36 months
UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018 — credit application and bureau data handling
FSMA 2000 — regulated activity; consumer credit must be FCA authorised

phases.name: Application
phases.description: Customer selects a credit card product from the bank's product range and submits an application. The customer provides income details, employment status, and consents to a hard credit check. An eligibility pre-check (bureau soft search indicator) assesses whether the customer is likely to be accepted before the hard search is committed. The application is created as ENT-022 CreditCardApplication.
key_activities: Customer browses card product range (ENT-024 CardProduct) — APR, rewards type, annual fee, eligibility criteria displayed
Customer selects product (product_id)
Customer submits application form: income_declared, employment_status, requested_limit (optional)
Eligibility pre-check: age >= 18 (GOV-005-R04), UK residency confirmed from Customer record, existing customer check
Customer consents to hard credit check (CCA 1974 s56 disclosure provided)
ENT-022 CreditCardApplication created (status: submitted)
EVT-040 CreditCardApplicationSubmitted published
phases.entry_criteria: Customer is an authenticated existing bank customer (PER-001, active Customer record in SVC-001). Customer is aged >= 18 and UK resident.
phases.exit_criteria: CreditCardApplication (ENT-022) created with status = 'submitted'. Hard credit check consent confirmed. EVT-040 published.
phases.sla: Real-time (< 2 seconds for form submission acceptance)
regulatory_touchpoints: CCA 1974 s56 — pre-contractual information (adequate explanations provided before consent to hard search)
CONC 5.2 — creditworthiness assessment; credit check consent required before hard search
Consumer Duty PS22/9 — product information must be clear, fair, and not misleading; APR prominently displayed
FCA CONC 3.5 — financial promotions for credit products (card comparison and promotional content)

phases.name: Eligibility and Credit Check
phases.description: SVC-003 performs automated eligibility checks and then requests a hard credit check from SVC-012 (Risk Engine, CAP-004) via async events. The credit check is a hard search that records a visible footprint on the customer's credit file. SVC-003 awaits the CreditCheckCompleted event before proceeding to decision. The cross-capability boundary between CAP-001 and CAP-004 is enforced: all communication with SVC-012 is via async events only.
key_activities: SVC-003 calls SVC-001 GET /customers/{id} to retrieve customer identity data for credit bureau submission (same-capability direct call)
Automated eligibility checks: existing customer status confirmed, no open bankruptcy/IVA flags, product eligibility criteria evaluated
EVT-041 CreditCheckRequested published to event bus (cross-capability to SVC-012, CAP-004)
SVC-012 calls credit bureau (Experian/Equifax/TransUnion) — hard search, bureau footprint recorded
SVC-012 returns EVT-042 CreditCheckCompleted with credit score, risk band, and recommended limit
SVC-003 consumes EVT-042, stores credit_assessment_reference on ENT-022
phases.entry_criteria: ENT-022 status = 'submitted'. Customer identity data retrievable from SVC-001.
phases.exit_criteria: EVT-042 CreditCheckCompleted received and consumed. Credit score and risk band stored on CreditCardApplication. Application transitions to 'assessment_complete'.
data_captured: credit_score (from bureau, stored as reference only)
phases.sla: < 30 seconds for automated eligibility; < 60 seconds for credit check response from SVC-012 (P95)
regulatory_touchpoints: CONC 5.3A — creditworthiness assessment must assess ability to make repayments in a sustainable manner
ICO Credit Reference Agencies guidance — hard search recorded on credit file; customer informed at application stage
UK GDPR Article 22 — automated decision-making: if solely automated, customer has right to contest; human review available for referred applications
CCA 1974 s157 — customer has right to know the name and address of any credit reference agency consulted

phases.name: Decision
phases.description: SVC-003 applies the bank's credit policy decisioning rules to the credit check result and income data to produce an approve, decline, or refer decision. On approval, a credit limit is assigned (lower of requested limit and risk-based recommended limit). On decline, the customer receives a CONC-compliant decline notice with right-to-know information. Referred applications are routed to a manual review queue.
key_activities: SVC-003 applies credit policy rules: credit score threshold, income-to-limit ratio, employment status policy
Approve path: credit limit assigned (min of requested_limit and recommended_credit_limit); ENT-022 status → 'approved'
Decline path: ENT-022 status → 'declined'; EVT-044 CreditCardDeclined published; CONC decline notice generated
Refer path: ENT-022 status → 'referred'; manual underwriter review queue; human decision within 2 business days
EVT-043 CreditCardApproved published (approve path) with assigned credit_limit
Customer notified of decision in-app and by email
phases.exit_criteria: Decision made: approved (EVT-043 published), declined (EVT-044 published), or referred (manual review queued). Customer notified.
phases.automation_level: full for approve/decline; semi-automated for refer (human review)
phases.sla: Automated decision: < 5 seconds after EVT-042 received. Referred applications: decision within 2 business days.
regulatory_touchpoints: CONC 7.3 — decline notice must be provided promptly; where declined based on credit reference data, customer has right to know which CRA was used (CCA 1974 s157)
UK GDPR Article 22 — automated decisions: on request, customer may request human review of automated decline
Consumer Duty PS22/9 — decline must not be presented in a way that is unclear or unfair; signpost to FOS if customer disputes decision
CONC 5.5 — credit limit: must be set at a level the customer can afford to repay; income-to-limit assessment documented

phases.name: Card Issuance
phases.description: Upon approval, SVC-003 creates the CreditCardAccount (ENT-023) and initiates card issuance. This phase is PCI DSS scoped: a card number (PAN) is generated by the card processing platform, immediately tokenised, and the raw PAN is never stored outside the PCI CDE. A virtual card is issued immediately; a physical card is dispatched to the customer's registered address for embossing. PIN generation is performed via a separate PCI-compliant PIN Management Service. The CreditCardIssued event payload contains card_number_token only — never the raw PAN.
key_activities: ENT-023 CreditCardAccount created (status: issued, credit_limit set, apr set, persistent_debt_flag: false)
PAN generated by card processing platform (Marqeta/Thredd or equivalent) within PCI CDE
PAN immediately tokenised → card_number_token stored on ENT-023 (raw PAN never persisted in SVC-003 or event payloads)
Virtual card credentials (card_number_token, expiry, CVV — scoped to PCI CDE for display) issued to customer via secure in-app viewer
Physical card embossing order submitted to fulfilment provider
PIN generation: customer sets PIN via encrypted PIN entry device (PCI PTS compliant); PIN block transmitted to HSM
EVT-045 CreditCardIssued published (payload: card_number_token only — PCI DSS compliant; no raw PAN)
phases.entry_criteria: ENT-022 status = 'approved'. EVT-043 consumed by issuance workflow.
phases.exit_criteria: ENT-023 CreditCardAccount created with status = 'issued'. Virtual card available in-app. Physical card dispatched. EVT-045 published.
data_captured: card_number_token (vault reference — PAN not stored outside CDE)
phases.sla: Virtual card: issued within 60 seconds of approval. Physical card: dispatched within 1 business day; delivered 3–5 business days.
pci_dss_controls: PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.3.1 — SAD (Sensitive Authentication Data including full PAN) not stored after authorisation
PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5 — PAN protected wherever stored; card_number_token used throughout SVC-003
PCI DSS v4.0 Req 4.2.1 — PAN encrypted in transit; TLS 1.2+ enforced
PCI DSS v4.0 Req 9.4 — physical card fulfilment: inventory and access controls at embossing facility
PCI DSS v4.0 Req 8.3 — PIN generation: only HSM-based PIN management; no clear-text PIN outside HSM
regulatory_touchpoints: PCI DSS v4.0 — full card issuance workflow scoped; card_number_token used exclusively outside CDE
PSR 2017 Reg. 100 — SCA for PIN set (at least two authentication factors at card activation)
Consumer Duty — clear, timely communication to customer about virtual vs. physical card availability

phases.name: Card Activation
phases.description: The customer activates the physical card. Activation is required before the card can be used for card-present or card-not-present transactions. Activation options: explicit activation via the banking app (preferred) or implicit activation on first transaction. SCA is applied to the activation step. Upon activation, ENT-023 status transitions to 'active'.
key_activities: Customer receives physical card
Customer activates card via banking app or online portal (SCA applied — knowledge + possession factors)
Alternative: first transaction implicitly activates card (card network authorisation triggers activation)
SVC-003 transitions ENT-023 status from 'issued' to 'active'
EVT-046 CreditCardActivated published
Customer notified: card active, credit limit confirmed, statement date communicated
phases.entry_criteria: ENT-023 status = 'issued'. Physical card received by customer (or first transaction attempted).
phases.exit_criteria: ENT-023 status = 'active'. EVT-046 CreditCardActivated published. Card available for transactions.
phases.sla: Explicit activation: < 5 seconds processing time after SCA. First transaction path: activation status updated within 100ms of authorisation decision.
regulatory_touchpoints: PSR 2017 Reg. 100 — SCA required for explicit card activation via remote channel
PCI DSS v4.0 — activation must not expose PAN; card_number_token used for all activation API calls
Consumer Duty — customer receives clear confirmation of activation; credit limit and first statement date communicated

phases.name: Ongoing Management
phases.description: The ongoing credit card account management lifecycle. Covers monthly statement generation, payment due date management, minimum payment calculation, and persistent debt monitoring required by FCA CONC 6.7.27–6.7.40. The persistent debt regime requires SVC-003 to monitor customers paying more in charges and interest than principal reduction over an 18-month rolling window and to intervene with prescribed communications. This phase is non-terminal — it runs for the life of the credit card account.
key_activities: Monthly statement generated (ENT-025 StatementCycle created): closing_balance, minimum_payment_due, payment_due_date
EVT-047 StatementGenerated published
Customer notified of statement availability and payment due date
Persistent debt monitoring: SVC-003 evaluates whether customer has paid more in interest/charges than principal over 18 rolling months
If persistent_debt_months >= 18: EVT-048 PersistentDebtAlertTriggered published; FCA-mandated intervention communication sent
If persistent_debt_months >= 27: second intervention — offer of repayment plan, credit limit suspension options
If persistent_debt_months >= 36: credit limit suspended; account referred to collections if no repayment arrangement
Direct debit payment collection via Bacs (minimum payment or full balance)
phases.entry_criteria: ENT-023 status = 'active'. First statement date reached (typically 30 days after activation).
phases.exit_criteria: This phase is ongoing for the life of the account. Terminal exit: account closed (balance cleared, customer request) or account written off (collections).
phases.automation_level: full (statement generation and persistent debt monitoring fully automated)
phases.sla: Statement generated on scheduled statement_date. Minimum payment due: 25 days after statement date (FCA CONC minimum). Persistent debt monitoring: run monthly on statement generation.
regulatory_touchpoints: FCA CONC 6.7.27–6.7.40 — persistent debt: 18-month trigger for first communication; 27-month for second; 36-month for credit limit suspension
FCA PS20/8 (persistent debt rules) — communication content prescribed; must include a repayment proposal
Consumer Credit Act 1974 s87 — default notice requirements before account suspension
FCA CONC 7.7 — minimum repayment amount: must cover all interest, fees, and minimum principal; cannot be set so low it leads to material debt growth
Consumer Duty PS22/9 — persistent debt outcome monitoring: board-level annual attestation
PCI DSS v4.0 — statements must not contain full PAN; card_number_token or masked PAN (last 4 digits) only

alternative_paths.name: Referred Application — Manual Review
alternative_paths.description: The automated credit decisioning engine cannot make an approve/decline decision with sufficient confidence (borderline credit score, complex income, or policy exception scenario). The application is routed to a manual credit review queue for a trained credit analyst to review.
key_differences: ENT-022 status transitions to 'referred' rather than 'approved' or 'declined'
Manual credit analyst reviews full application and credit report
Decision within 2 business days (Consumer Duty: timely outcome)
If approved: joins PH-026 (Card Issuance) from the manual decision point
Analyst decision is documented as human override in audit trail

alternative_paths.name: Balance Transfer Application
alternative_paths.description: Customer applies for a card specifically to transfer an existing balance from another lender. Balance transfer fee applies (percentage of amount transferred). Promotional balance transfer APR (often 0%) applies for an introductory period. Assessed under same credit decisioning rules with additional consideration of total indebtedness.
key_differences: Application includes balance_transfer_amount and source_lender fields
Affordability assessment considers total indebtedness including transfer amount
Credit limit must accommodate balance transfer amount
Promotional APR period tracked on ENT-023; reverts to standard APR at promotional expiry
Balance transfer executed after activation: SVC-003 instructs CHAPS/Bacs payment to source lender

exception_paths.name: Credit Decline
exception_paths.description: Automated decisioning or manual review results in a credit decline. Customer's credit score is below the bank's policy threshold or income is insufficient to support the requested credit limit.
resolution_options: Decline notice issued with right to know which CRA was used (CCA 1974 s157)
Customer signposted to free debt advice services (MoneyHelper) per Consumer Duty
Customer may request a Subject Access Request (SAR) for their credit file data
If decline is based solely on automated processing: customer may request human review (UK GDPR Art. 22)

exception_paths.name: PCI DSS Issuance Failure
exception_paths.description: Card number generation, tokenisation, or PIN generation fails within the PCI CDE. Partial issuance states must be handled safely — no dangling PAN references outside the CDE.
resolution_options: SVC-003 rolls back ENT-023 to 'approval_pending' status if PAN generation fails before tokenisation
Retry issuance workflow (idempotent on application_id) up to 3 times
If retry exhausted: alert card operations team; customer notified of delay; no PAN fragment persisted outside CDE
Audit trail maintained for all issuance failure events per PCI DSS Req 10.2

exception_paths.name: Persistent Debt — 36-Month Suspension
exception_paths.description: Customer has been in persistent debt for 36 months despite receiving intervention communications at 18 and 27 months. FCA rules require the bank to suspend credit limit increases and may require suspension of the credit facility itself.
resolution_options: Credit limit suspended: no new purchases until persistent debt resolved
Repayment plan offered: accelerated repayment to reduce persistent debt
If no repayment arrangement: account referred to collections team
Default notice issued under CCA 1974 s87 before formal default
Debt written off after 6-year limitation period (Limitation Act 1980) if unrecoverable

exception_paths.name: Customer Withdrawal (Right to Withdraw)
exception_paths.description: Customer exercises their statutory 14-day right to withdraw from the regulated credit agreement under CCA 1974 s66A. The right runs from the day the credit agreement is entered into or from when the customer receives the agreement terms, whichever is later.
resolution_options: Customer notifies bank in writing or via app within 14 days
Customer must repay any credit already drawn down (plus interest accrued) within 30 days
CreditCardAccount closed; card_number_token invalidated in tokenisation vault
Hard search footprint on credit file remains (cannot be reversed once recorded at bureau)
No penalty for exercising statutory right of withdrawal
